text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning.

- Irregular trade in shares by a former top manager may have costed Oslo brokerhouse Noka Securites at least 50 million crowns. Yesterday, Noka discontinued business and the economic crime squad is investigating the irregular trade.
- Between 25,000 and 35,000 Norwegians aged 15 to 25 suffer from eating disorders. Hospital personnel and teachers must learn more about the problem, the State Nourishment Council says.
- For the first time a Norwegian must serve a prison term for illegally copying software for personal computers. The man was sentenced to 120 days behind bars.
- A total of 113 workers will lose their jobs now that shipbuilding and engineering firm Kvaerner ASA wants to shut down its Kvaerner Kimek shipyard in Kirkenes, northern Norway.
- An F-16 jet fighter hit an electricity line and crashed into the sea, but the pilot parachuted to safety. It seems the pilot did not read his map properly before he took off.
- Insurance company Storebrand will now seek legal advice to remove all doubts stirred around the status of its preference shares by industrial group Aker RGI.
- Higher oil prices increased the first-quarter profits of Statoil, the Norwegian state-owned oil company.
- A new gas market opens up for Norway after the British and Norwegian governments reached agreement on revisions to the treaty governing operations of the Frigg gas pipeline.
- Brokerhouse Noka Securites is bankrupt. The economic crime squad is questioning its top manager for losses that could amount to more than 100 million crowns.

- The best lawyers in the country are now working intensively to save the proposed merger between insurer Storebrand and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse after industrial group Aker RGI raised doubts about whether Storebrand can redeem preference shares.
- The power struggle between the banks continues. Fokus Bank yesterday did not signal to Den norske Bank that it is giving up the fight for mortgage lender BNbank.
- The EU Commission threatens Norway with legislation against dumping of oil platforms in the sea.
- Telecommunications group Nera is struggling with lower income and fewer orders. The share fell on the Oslo Bourse after the company reported lower first-quarter profits yesterday.
